summary: Audited all three originally reported call sites. Janus remains CPU-only and its tuple-form candidate was slower, the former Gemma call no longer exists, and Phi now uses an equivalent fixed-size bucketize mapping that avoids nonzero and its interval temporary.

tests.what_was_measured: 19 equivalence and metadata cases covering empty, sparse, dense, boundary, tail, and attention-window inputs against the pre-change interval/nonzero reference.
Actual Janus nonzero input device, Phi output metadata, controlled CPU candidate timings, and queued-work GPU synchronization timings on the assigned MI355X.
Python syntax and patch whitespace validation.

gpu_evidence: On AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, both GPU nonzero forms took a median 41.51-41.53 ms behind a calibrated 41.52 ms queued sleep, while fixed-output bucketize and add returned in about 0.005 ms.
remaining_limitations: The stale Gemma nonzero call was source/history verified only because it is absent from current main; no Gemma model-weight run was applicable.
Janus used the actual processor method with deterministic fake tokenizer and image processor inputs, not model weights.
Unrelated nonzero sites introduced elsewhere after the original report were listed during audit but were not mechanically changed or claimed as resolved.
